title: India-China Relations: Borders and Strategic Competition

scenes.text: Can two Asian giants resolve their disputed Himalayan boundary and strategic rivalry?
scenes.narration: Imagine two ancient civilisations aiming for an Asian century, yet unable to agree where their shared border lies! That unresolved boundary has turned potential partnership into decades of intense strategic rivalry.

scenes.text: Two apartment neighbours sharing a corridor while trading groceries yet arguing over property lines.
scenes.narration: Think of this through an everyday analogy of two flat owners in a housing society. They exchange groceries warmly in the lobby, yet argue furiously whenever someone puts a flowerpot in the common corridor!

scenes.narration: Here is the trick to remembering their complex history. After early friendship pacts broke down into the 1962 war, both sides built military agreements like the 2013 pact to keep border peace.

scenes.heading: Disputed Border Sectors

columns.title: Western Sector
items: All-weather route connecting Tibet and Xinjiang

scenes.narration: Look at how the dispute divides across two main sectors. In the east, China rejects the British McMahon Line in Arunachal Pradesh, while in the west, it controls Aksai Chin to connect Tibet with Xinjiang.

scenes.heading: Three-Phase Border Resolution Process
scenes.narration: Notice how both nations agreed on guiding principles to resolve this fairly. Although initial principles and ground work are complete, the final phase of exchanging maps remains stalled by mutual mistrust.

scenes.heading: Strategic Rivalry Beyond the Border
items: Brahmaputra river dams raise water diversion concerns
Growing bilateral trade deficit facing Indian exports
Heavy Chinese infrastructure investments across South Asia
scenes.narration: Now see how competition expands far beyond the mountains. India worries about upstream Brahmaputra dams, a widening trade deficit where India buys much more than it sells, and growing Chinese projects across South Asia.

items: Contested eastern and western sectors remain unresolved

Competition extends across rivers, trade, and neighbours
scenes.narration: Here are the three big takeaways to remember. Master the disputed boundary sectors, the vital peace agreements maintaining stability, and the broader strategic race across the region.
